articleTitle: New method for electro-optic linearization of external modulators
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: We report a novel linearization technique for Mach-Zehnder waveguide modulators which uses an electro-optic circuit to cancel all orders of distortion in the optical domain. The circuit has demonstrated 56dB CNR and 65 dB CTB with 80 NTSC carriers modulated at 4.5% optical modulation index and canceling distortion products by 35 dB.

articleTitle: High Performance Fiber Optic Links using Fabry Perot Lasers in Wireless Signal Distribution
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Link performance at 900 MHz and 2 GHz will be discussed using 1300nm Strained Layer Multi Quantum Well Fabry Perot (SL-MQW-FP) lasers. These lasers, that have shown excellent performance in local loop digital system environments, can also demonstrate excellent performance in analog system applications. Noise performance and linearity will be discussed under a variety of conditions: fiber length ranging from 0 to 25 km and over varying operating temperatures ranges. The performance will be contrasted with links using DFB lasers and performance limitations will be discussed.

articleTitle: Analog Optoelectronic Module Development TRIP
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: The goal of this TRP is to apply novel packaging techniques and low cost manufacturing processes to develop affordable analog OE modules that will enable a new infrastructure for future broadband networks and systems serving both military and commercial markets.

articleTitle: GaAs HBT Technology: Devices and Models for High Speed Circuit Design
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Characteristics of GaAs HBTs - in the laboratory and in manufacturing - are reviewed. Departures from SPICE BJT models, and consequences for circuit design, are discussed. Approaches for device speed imporvement are highlighted, emphasizing higher ft and lower Cbc.

articleTitle: A Vision for Residential broadband Services: ATM-to-the-home
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: A vision of a residential broadband network architecture based on ATM-to-the-home architecture is presented. It will be shown to satisfy the diverse networking requirements for interactive broadband services and applications envisioned for residential broadband networks. It explains in detail why ATM-to-the-home is not only the best technical solution available, but also the best strategic solution for deploying residential broadband services.

articleTitle: Ill-V ICs for Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Summary form only given, as follows. Commercial communications systems are rapidly expanding to the RF and millimeter-wave spectrum. The impacts of recent advances in the Ill-V compound semiconductor devices and integrated circuits on modern high speed wireless communications systems will be illustrated in a prototype microwave communication link.

articleTitle: Modular, scalable, and space qualified lasercorn technology for the gil
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Satellite systems are a key element of the NIVGII. There are many applications for which satellite systems are the best or only way to achieve information distribution goals. New systems, such as Hughes’ SPACEWAY, will meet GI1 needs in an affordable, ubiquitous manner.

articleTitle: High Speed ICs for Large Capacity Optical Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Optical amplifiers have accelerated research on high-speed lightwave communication systems. However, R &D activities for high speed ICs are still essential. This paper is focused on high-speed ICs for constructing 10 Gb/s transmission systems.

articleTitle: Optically Controlled Phased Array Antennas for Army Communications on-the-Move
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: The intensity and speed of Desert Storm highlighted the need for communications on-the-move. The capabilities offered by optically controlled phased arrays for satellite and terrestrial communications can contribute greatly in meeting this challenge.

articleTitle: Broadband Subcriber Access Systems and Technologies
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: One of the most challenging tasks in establishing a new gllobal information infrastructure is rebuilding the subscriber access network. The old circuit-switched telephony network must be replaced, requiring an enormous investment in new broadband circuitlpacket multi-service networks. This presentation describes the competing systems and technologies that will enable the transition to occur.

articleTitle: Architechture and Control for Multiservices Broadband Access Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: This talk will describe the services (digital video, telephony, data access for internet and work at home) that are desirable, review the more popular architectures (HFC, FTTC, FTTH), and discuss the software architectural issues as well.

articleTitle: A Wide Bandwidth Monolithic Long Wavelength MODFET/ MSM Photoreceiver
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: A long-wavelength photoreceiver using quarter-micron gatelength lattice-matched InAiAs/ InGaAs/InP MODFETs and a MSM-PD has been fabricated and characterized. This photoreceiver exhibited a wide bandwidth of 15 GHz.

articleTitle: The role of satellites in the global information infrastructure
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Satellite systems are a key element of the NIVGII. There are many applications for which satellite systems are the best or only way to achieve information distribution goals. New systems, such as Hughes’ SPACEWAY, will meet GI1 needs in an affordable, ubiquitous manner.

articleTitle: Cost-effective Fiber-to-the-Home System, and Device Technologies for Multimedia Access Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: NTT has announced a deployment plan to introduce fiber cables in subscriber access networks. In order to promote the plan, intensive development of the FITH systems and the components is currently being carried out. The most important and difficult problem to overcome is to develop a cost-effective FITH systems to provide both telephone and multimedia services.

articleTitle: Burst Mode Receivers for Fiber Optic Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Burst mode receivers are being used increasingly for multipoint-to-point fiber optic networks including local loop Passive Optical Networks (PONS) and Local Area Networks (LANs). In this talk a burst mode receiver implementation including DC restoration, amplitude detection and clock recovery will be described. The system will be compared to alternative burst mode receiver systems and realizations.

articleTitle: System Design and Test Results of a Wideband Photonic Conformal Array
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: This talk is an introduction to the optical control of an L-band 96-element array using fiber optic links and a photonic beam forming network for wide instantaneous bandwidth calibration data, range effects, and measured antenna patterns over wideband and +,60° scans will be reported.

articleTitle: An Improved Model of Blocking Probability in All-Optical Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: We have developed a model of blocking probability in an All-Optical Network (AON) without wavelength changers and tested this model against simulations. The new model is an improvement of a model first proposed in [l].

articleTitle: HLAN - An Architecture for Optical Multi-Access Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Many discussions in the recent literature address issues in designing architectures for high speed optical multiaccess networks in the presence of long propagation delays, e.g. [1,2,3]. There are several diffEulties in creating such architectures. One difficulty is to design solutions that support both guaranteed bandwidth (GBW) services and random access bandwidth-on-demand (BOD) services.

articleTitle: Microwave frequency synthesis using injection locked laser comb line selection
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Microwave frequency synthesis can be realised by mixing the output of two or more DFB lasers injection locked to the same optical comb. The noise and stability problems of this approach are studied.

articleTitle: The Case for Opaque Multiwavelength Optical Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM) now seems certain to play a leading role in public telecommunications networks of the future. What is unclear, however, is whether these WDM networks will be "transparent," i.e., whether their signals will travel from source to destination through a sequence of intervening nodes with little or no optoelectronic conversion along the way. In this work we consider "opaque" WDM networks, in which network elements include optoelectronic conversion and signal regeneration along the path, thus preventing accumulation of impairments.

articleTitle: An InP-Based HBT 1x8 OEIC Array for a WDM Network
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: An eight-channel optical receiver front-end array has been designed and fabricated using InP-based HBT, IC technology. The 2.5 Gb/s circuits include photodetectors constructed from HBT base-collector junctions, transimpedance amplifiers, and differential output stages.

articleTitle: A novel photonic oscillator
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Traditional RF oscillators cannot meet all requirements of photonic RF systems. Because photonic systems contain RF signals in both optical and electrical domains, an ideal oscillator for the photonic systems should be able to generate directly electrical signals, as well as signals as the optical subcarrier.

articleTitle: Ultrafast High Power Photodetectors
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Ultrafast photodetectors with high optical saturation powers are highly desirable for analog fiber optic links and optically controlled phased array antennas [l]. Though high speed photodetectors are now commercially available, their saturation powers are generally limited to a few milliwatts. High power photodetectors with surface-illumination [2] and waveguide [3] geometries have been reported.

articleTitle: High-Speed Travelling-Wave Photodetectors, Modulators and Switches
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: The design and properties of travelling-wave optoelectronic devices using coupled coplanar or microstrip and optical waveguides are, discussed. Theoretical and experimental results of high-speed photodetectors, electrooptical modulators, and optical switches are summarized. Special emphasis is futher laid upon field induced waveguiding phenomena.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis in the Linear Lightwave Network
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: This paper proposes an algorithm for fault localization in a Linear Lightwave Network (LLN). A LLN is an all-optical network using Linear Dividers Combiners (LDCs) as network nodes. These LDCs can perform either wavelength or waveband selective linear operations on optical signals including controllable power dividing and combining [l].

articleTitle: Dynamic Range of Analog Optical Links: Do Optical Amplifiers Help?
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Applications of analog optical links include CATV distribution, phased array antennas, antenna remoting, and as backbone for wireless communication systems (see for example [1]).

articleTitle: 60GHz Polymer Electro-optic Phase Modulators
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Direct modulation has a limited bandwidth and requires high quality, low chirp semiconductor lasers. External optical modulation permits the development of low cost, high frequency optical fiber data links using relatively simple semiconductor lasers.

articleTitle: Time Coherent Ultra-Wideband Pulse Generation Using Photoconductive Switching
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Jitter-free photoconductive (PC) switching is employed to generate a jam-resistant, time-coherent ultra wideband (UWB) pulse train. The power from multiple PC switch triggered antenna elements is combined in free space to produce a steerable UWB beam.

articleTitle: 10Gb/s GaAs driver IC and 5.7V/sun/sub p-p/ output hybrid hermetic module for extemal light modulators
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: A great deal of effort has been recently made around the world to develop 10Gb/ s (OC-192) fiber-optic transmission devices and equipment. In the transmitter side, a fiber dispersion issue prompts a use of external light modulators, necessitating a large voltage-swing output driver.

articleTitle: Wide Bandwidth InAlAs/InGaAs Monolithic PIN-HBT Photoreceiver
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: InP-based high performance integrated photoreceivers working at speeds of 10 Gb/s and higher are currently being developed for applications in long-distance optical communications.

articleTitle: Economical Applications of All-Optical Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: The emergence of optical amplifiers, wavelength division multiplexing capabilities, and more recently, optical cross connection for application in fiber optic networks has popularized the concept of an all-optical network to provide a flexible physical layer for transport networks capable of delivering the very large capacities required. It remains a challenge to not only overcome the considerable technological challenges toward this end, but also to understand applications of these technologies and the networks they enable and the intrinsic economic benefits they will bring to network operators and their end users. This paper considers the economic incentives for developing all-optical network capabilities.

articleTitle: Optical Fiber Based Interferoceiver
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Sampling oscilloscopes based on fast samplers are the common diagnostic instruments for deciphering transient events. By adding a faster sampler and sampling bridge, a sampling oscilloscope will increase its capabilities. However, as the capabilities increase, a major problem arises, that is often referred to as the throughput limitation. Interesting questions follow: such as do we have other choices, and can we circumvent the throughput limitation? We do have a choice. The newly advanced technology on optical fibers provides us a completely novel alternative.

articleTitle: High-speed Monolithically Integrated pin-HEMT Photoreceivers
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: High-speed optical transmission technology has rapidly developed to the point that 10 Gbit/s is possible, and transmission experiments at 20 Gbit/s are currently being carried out using intensity modulation/ direct detection (IM/DD) schemes [1].

articleTitle: Organic Electroluminescent Devices
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Organic electroluminescence (EL) has received considerable attention in recent years. 1-3 This thin film emissive technology is attractive for display applications for reasons of high efficiency, low voltage, ease of fabrication, and potential for full color.

articleTitle: Optical Beam Forming Network with True-Time Delay Using Mode-Locked Supermodes and Dispersive Fiber
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: The conventional techniques to measure the spatial distribution of electromagnetic radiation are based on the serial recording the radiation from pixels by a single detector or on the parallel recording by a detector array.

articleTitle: High-Reliability Self-Aligned InGaP/GaAs HBTs for Lightwave Communications
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: The development of advanced IC technologies is a key factor in high-speed light wave communication systems, operating at over lO-Gb/s. 111-V based heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) ICs are very promising candidates because of their excellent high-speed characteristics. l)

articleTitle: Low Phase-Noise Millimeter-Wave Signal Generation Using Semiconductor Lasers
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: There is presently much effort devoted towards the generation of millimeter-wave (mm-wave) modulated optical signals for applications including optically fed mm-wave wireless systems and optical phased arrays. This paper presents some recent results on the generation of stable and low phase-noise mm-wave signals using semiconductor lasers.

articleTitle: Autonomous Timing Determination in a Time-Slotted WDM All-Optical Network
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: There are several network services provided by the 20 wavelength all-optical network (AON) testbed deployed in the Boston metropolitan area[ 11 by the Consortium on Wideband All- Optical Networks. One is a scheduled time and wavelength division multiplexed service which supports multiple simultaneous and independently optically routed connections for users with data rates variable from -10 Mbps to 1.244 Gbps. A key feature of this T D W M service is the time-slot synchronization required for the efficient use of network resources, especially when data is transmitted in short high-rate bursts or time-slots. We demonstrate autonomous transmitter/receiver synchronization over a metropolitan area testbed. This allows signals from widely distributed sources to mesh without collision on common a wavelength at a common fiber, router or other time-shared network resource.

articleTitle: Electronic & optoelectronic components for fiber transmission at bandwidths approaching 100 ghz
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Fiber-optic data transmission systems are evolving rapidly. 10 Gb/s time-division- multiplexed (TDM) systems are approaching deployment) and there is extensive research on 40 Gb/s transmission.

articleTitle: Lsi chip set for 10Gb/s optical transmission system
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: High-speed transmission capability in the 10Gb/s range has been target of the recent transmission system developments[1-4].

articleTitle: The Luminescent Process in Organic Light Emitting Devices
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Understanding the electroluminescent (EL) process in organic light emitting devices is very important for the rational design of optimized chromophores for use in organic LEDs. By comparing solution and solid state fluorescence spectra, it has been shown that molecularly localized or Frenkel excitons are responsible for the EL output.

articleTitle: <10Hz linewidth optical millimetre-wave source for fibre-radio systems using a dual mode dfb semiconductor laser
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: We demonstrate the generation of millimetre-wave signals with <10Hz linewidth and with 500MHz locking range using a dual mode semiconductor laser. A subharmonic drive signal phase locks the beat signal produced by heterodyning the two modes. Recently frequencies in the millimetre-wave band have been proposed to meet the future demand for broadband wireless access networks. Frequencies at 62-63GHz and 65-66GHz have been allocated in Europe for the Mobile Broadband System (MBS) and the 40GHz region has been identified for longer range (up to 1km) applications such as video distribution. To enable this technology with low cost, fibre distribution of radio signals at 40GHz and 60-70GHz will be required. Very few optical sources cap of modulation at these frequencies have been demonstrated [1,2].

articleTitle: Optical Cross-Connect Based on WDM and Space Division Multiplexing
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: It is well known that wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) can be used for optical cross-connects [1][2]. To construct a large scale optical cross-connect with WDM, we have to consider reusing a limited number of wavelengths in some ways.

articleTitle: CORD - Toward Optically Transparent, WDM Packet Switched Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: In an optically transparent network, payload data are transported from source to destination completely in the optical domain. A primary advantage of optical transparency is avoiding the throughput limitation imposed by intermediate electronic switching, routing, and optical to electrical and electrical to optical conversions. An additional benefit of optically transparent networks is their indifference to modulation format and bit rate, allowing them to efficiently evolve to handle higher speed and heterogeneous traffic.

articleTitle: High Speed HBT-based OEIC Photoreceivers for long wavelength system applications
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Monolithically integrated photoreceivers have been pursed as an advantageous alternative for use in high speed long wavelength transmission systems. One potential transistor technology compatible with opto-electronic integrated circuits (OEICs) in the InP/InGaAs material system is the heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT).

articleTitle: Comparison of Low Cost Printed Antennas Suitable for Optical Fiber Microcellular Radio Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Microcellular systems have been proposed as an ideal solution to the ever increasing demand for mobile and personal communications. System capacity in these networks which are composed of small-size cells with several hundred meter diameter communication range is greatly increased due to improved frequency reuse.

articleTitle: Toward Multimedia Applications on the STARNET WDM Network
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Technological progress and increased user needs have provided the primary impetus for development of high-speed networks which simultaneously deliver real-time services in addition to standard file and data transfer services. Real-time services must provide not only bandwidth, but must also limit latency in order to meet quality of service requirements. Typical real-time services include compressed voice and video.

articleTitle: Bidirectional transparent optical networks
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: In this paper, based on bidirectional optical amplifiers and n couplers, we propose a bidirectional transparent (BTL) network configuration. Compared to the MPL and SLB schemes, the BTL structure can save much optical fiber and optical filters.

articleTitle: Transmitters, receivers and detectors for high speed parallel optical interconnect links
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: The increasing need for higher bandwidth interconnections between computer links, ATM switches, multimedia applications, and telecommunication switches has led to a large amount of research on high speed optical interconnects.

articleTitle: A Novel Multi-functional Optoelectronic Device for Large Scale Integration: a Detector, an Electronic Transistor and a Laser Diode in One
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Monolithic integration of a detector, an electronic transistor and a light emitter on a single chip, is one of the most attractive configurations for high-speed optical communication and information processing systems. A major difficulty encountered when integrating these devices is the incompatibility among fabrication steps of the three devices. To eliminate this problem, we present a novel optoelectronic device with large functionality and simple integration technology. It can be used as a detector, an electronic transistor and a light emitter.

articleTitle: Data Networking Services in the Enterprise
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Two significant changes are occurring in enterprise local area networking. They are networks are increasing being used to support mission critical business applications and the networking technology is in transition from shared media hubs and router micro-segmentation to switching for increased performance. Another change that is anticipated is the wide spread use of real time multi-media applications such as broadcast video, collaborative interactive computing and video teleconferencing. These changes require data networks to move to a more service oriented model than is currently associated with enterprise LANs. The services are in the areas of transport, operations and policy services.

articleTitle: A Simple Reconfigurable Antenna
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: When a semiconductor is irradiated with light or electrons of sufficient energy, the irradiated part will become conducting. This well-known mechanism can be used to create antennas with conducting parts controlled by the irradiating source, and structures reconfigurable by changing the irradiation patterns.

articleTitle: 10 Gb/s Optical Transmission using a Silicon Bipolar Chipset
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: A 10 Gb/s silicon chip set including a 8:1 MUX, a 1.8 DMUX, a dynamic divider, and circuits for clock recovery is described. Results from optical transmission experiments utilizing dispersion compensation techniques such as prechirp and MSSI, and bridging distances from 50 to 100 km, will be presented.

articleTitle: Wide dynamic range fiber optic links utilizing pre-distortion and dssc approach
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: During the last few years AEL has developed a new approach for modulating optical carriers with RF data while maximizing the SFDR and minimizing the required RF gain. This approach which utilizes a unique optical DSSC modulation technique will enhance the performance of antenna remoting systems and minimize the requirements on the RF circuitry while achieving state of the art dynamic range performance. In addition, a RF pre-distortion approach has been developed for operation up to 1 GHz and is currently a commercial product line.

articleTitle: Proposal for Using High Density Wavelength Switching for All-Optical Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: WDM systems are widely considered to be the vehicle for future all-optical networks. However, the prevailing approaches to this problem are based on the assumption that only low tens (say 20) of wavelength can be practical employed.

articleTitle: Vacuum Deposited Organic Light Emitting Devices for Full-Color Flat Panel Display Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Recently, both polymeric and molecular organic multilayer structures have been extensively investigated for their potential application to lightweight, inexpensive, full color flat panel displays. In this paper, we discuss the physical origin of electroluminescence in such devices, and its implications for the limits to device efficiency, operating voltage and device lifetime.

articleTitle: Epitaxial liftoff as a method-of manufacturing large area crystalline silicon transistor arrays for AMLCD's
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Crystalline silicon transistors offer better performance and higher speeds than amorphous or poly-silicon transistors. This leads to higher resolution, larger displays, and better performance of the AMLCD. Using pre-fabricated crystalline silicon devices allows for the advantage of more complex circuit design within the pixel such as the incorporation of storage capacitors, or multi-device circuits at each pixel. This technique also offers a simplified, lower cost alternative to present production processes.

articleTitle: Recent Progress in the Consortium an Wideband All-Optical Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Optical communication technology wilt play an increasing role in the global information infrastructure. There are major efforts around the world focused on developing high capacity ground and space based optical communication systems. We will review the status of the Consortium on Wideband All-Optical Networks. The goal of this Consortium is to develop architecture and technology for scalable and wideband WDM optical networks and to demonstrate the architectural principles in a test-bed. This test-bed is now deployed in the Boston metropolitan area and we are in the process of characterizing the network and running experimental applications.

articleTitle: System aspects of fiber optic-RF links for communications
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Optical fiber can provide a convenient low loss means of distributing RF, microwave, and millimeter wave signals in communications. The principal impediment to the wider use of this technology is the cost of the components, particularly those !hat constitute the optical transmitters and receivers.

articleTitle: Design and Measurement of Electrical Properties of a Traveling-Wave InGaAs/InGaAlAs Quantum Well Waveguide
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Lumped-element modulators that are compact can reach capacitance-limited electrical bandwidths as high as 40 GHz. Using quantum wells as the active material drive voltages are on the order of a few volts.

articleTitle: Ultrahigh Speed HBT ICs for TDM Lightwave Communication
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: We present some key 10-40 Gb/s circuits for Time Division Multiplexing (TDM) optical fiber transmission. These include 4:1 multiplexer, 1:4 demultiplexer, limiting amplifier, decision circuit, and differentiation and rectification circuitry for clock recovery.

articleTitle: Design Techniques for Non-Oversampled, Instantaneously Locked Clock and Data Recovery Circuits - An Overview
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Traditional narrow-band clock recovery circuits such as those based on LC tanks, SAW filters or PLLs suffer from the fundamental limitation of locking (reaching steady-state operation) slowly compared to the input data rate. This is inconsequential in classical digital links where phase-coherent data flows continuously. However, if data arrives in asynchronous packets, as it does in modern communication systems such as PON’s (Passive Optical Networks), long locking times cause significant penalties in the transmission efficiency. For burst-mode applications new clock recovery methods with greater acquisition agility are needed.

articleTitle: Thin-film-edge emitter field emitter arrays for avionics display backlight applications
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: We report the feasibility of thin-film-edge emitter devices as electron sources for high brightness cathodoluminescent lamp for possible backlighting of AMLCD. This lamp promises to be of high brightness, high luminous efficiency , temperature invariant with uniform diffuse light output. The thin-film-edge FEA lamp requires less electronic control circuitry leading to lower system costs.

articleTitle: High Power Photodetectors for Space Communications Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: High power photodetectors in coplanar waveguide and distributed traveling-wave structures have been under development for communications applications. The distributed photodetectors demonstrated 70% efficiency with a linear response upto 25 mW of optical power input.

articleTitle: Integrated Circuit Packet Receivers for TDM Passive Optical Networks
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: A form of optical communications with increasing commercial importance requires passive sharing of optical fiber among several optoelectronic sources and detectors. One example is the “Passive Optical Network” ON) illustrated in Figure 1. Here, several terminal units (Optical Network Units - OW) are linked by passively connected optical fibers to a service provider (Optical Subscriber Unit - OSU) that is in tum the gateway to the outside network.

articleTitle: Prospects for Ultra-Fast CMOS Circuits
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: An Overview of how the advances in deep submicron CMOS technologies, coupled with circuit design techniques and higher levels of integration, provide excellent opportunities for the ultra fast CMOS circuits to play an important role in very high speed lightwave communication systems will be presented.

articleTitle: Efficiency Limits for Emissive Polymer LEDs
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Measurements of conjugated polymer photoluminescence yield are often motivated by their implications for the emissive efficiency of electroluminescent devices based upon the same material. We report studies of phenylenevinylene polymers that enable us to identify two important mechanisms, one intrinsic and one extrinsic, which reduce the luminescence efficiency. We also show that one of the premises underlying the presumed correlation between electroluminescence and photoluminescence quantum yields is incorrect.

articleTitle: Design and fabrication of single side band (ssb) optical modulator
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: This paper concentrates on the design and fabrication of the various components of a SSB optical modulator. The material used is x-cut, Mg-doped, Lithium Niobate (LiNbO3). The optical modulators are fabricated using the annealed proton exchange technique.

articleTitle: II-VI blue/green laser diodes
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: due to a burn-out at the evaporated gold contacts. By 1992 progress was made towards overcoming the lack of an ohmic contact to p-ZnSe. Two methods currently employed to provide contacts to p-ZnSe include the use of an intermediate layer of HgSe to reduce the Schottky barrier height as employed by the group at NC State in their LED devices, as well as the pseudograded Zn(Se,Te) contact proposed by the authors'. The Zn(Se,Te) graded contacts have proven a key element in reaching the objective of room temperature CW operation of 508nm laser diodes. In addition to their use in laser devices, the fact that the ohmic behavior of the Zn(Se,Te) graded contact persists to cryogenic temperatures permitted temperature-dependant Hall measurements to be performed.

articleTitle: Routing-and Switching for Optical Transport Networks in RACE
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: In future telecommunications, optical circuit- and packet-techniques will perform routing and switching to ensure simultaneously transparency, optical continuity and bandwidth granularity. Network architectures, system demonstrators and advanced technologies have been developed in Europe under RACE to study and implement future high performance optical transport networks.

articleTitle: SiGe HBT ICs for 20-Gb/s Optical Communication System
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Rapid progress in multimedia communication requires large capacity optical transmission lines over 10 Gb/s. One of the candidates considered for use in the forthcoming high speed transmission systems is a 2OGb/s optical IM-DD transmission system.

articleTitle: The design of laser diodes with low distortion for application in large bandwidth catv-systems
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: The design of DFB laser diodes with low distortion is of crucial importance for optical CATV transmission systems. As the number of requested channels still increases, a low distortion over an increasing bandwidth is needed.

articleTitle: High Frequency Optically Coherent Analog Antenna Link with True Time Delay
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: There has been much interest in the use of high bandwidth, light weight optical fiber to implement true time delays in future generations of phased array 4qeq4[1-2]. Among the various architectures proposed, the coherent detection architecture[2] offers several important advantages including high channel packing density, excellent SNR and the flexibility needed in large - scale phased array radar antenna systems. This type of system is very compact, transmitting several hundred delays to different antenna elements using a single fiber.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Self-Filtering Effect in WDM Systems with Cascaded EDFAs
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: In recent years, EDFAs have played an indispensable role jn WDM applications [1]. However, there is an issue that remains: the EDFA gain is wavelength-dependent, and a small gain imbalance is unavoidable.

articleTitle: Control of the emission pattern and strongly directed emission from multilayer organic EL diodes
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Much progress has been shown in R&D of conventional organic electroluminescent (EL) diodes in which a variety of organic materials have been used as an emissive or a charge transport layer. Thickness of the organic layers in the EL diodes constructed from vacuum-sublimed films is generally less than the wavelength of the emitted light.

articleTitle: Scalability of Optical Multi-Wavelength Switching Networks: Power Budget Analysis
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Scalability with bit rate, number of wavelengths, number of input/output fibres per node is analysed , giving networks with very high data capacity (2000 Tb/s.km). Limits are optical noise accumulation, gain saturation, Raman scattering, dispersion.

articleTitle: The Role of OEICs in Commercial Applications
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: The concept of Opto-Electronic Integrated Circuits (OEICs) has been around for many years but only in the last few years has it seen extensive commercial application.

articleTitle: High-Brightness Blue & Green LEDs Grown by MBE on ZnSe Substrates
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: High-brightness blue and green tight-emitting diodes (LEDs) operating at peak wavelengths in the range 489 -514 nm have been successfully synthesized, processed, and tested. The high-brightness LEDs are Il-VI heterostructures grown by molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) at NCSU using (100) ZnSe substrates produced at Eagle-Picher Laboratory by the Seeded Physical Vapor Transport (SPVT TM) process.

articleTitle: Generation of microwave signals by electrically locked mode beating in an OEIC DFB laser with extended cavity
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: A simple method of generating microwave signals by using a single DFB laser integrated with an extended cavity is presented. High spectral purity is achieved by locking to harmonics of an electrical drive signal applied to the laser bias current.

articleTitle: Transmissive Star Coupler based Experimental Dense WDM-LANs interconnected via a Central Node
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: For future access- and local area networks the simultaneous transmission of many high bitrate channels will be necessary. A promising candidate to fulfill this requirement is the dense WDM (DWDM) technique. DWDM-LANs with different network topologies have been proposed and were investigated [e.g. 1, 2, 31 as well as the all-optical interconnection of LA" with reflective star couplers 141. This paper reports the in [5] proposed all-optical interlink of modified transmissive star coupler based experimental DWDM-LANs with isolated expansion ports and a channel spacing of 9 GHz. Each LAN has four fully engineered, microprocessor controlled and absolute frequency stabilized subscriber stations. As well heterodyne as direct detection receivers with fixed and tunable filters and optical preamplifiers are implemented.

articleTitle: Combination of fiber laser, amplifier, and logic gate for ultrafast switching in TDM networks
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: We are working toward combining all-optical soliton logic gates, erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (EDFA'S), and erbium-doped fiber lasers (EDFL's) to perform ultrafast serial processing in networks.

articleTitle: A low cost, high performance optical interconnect
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: The driving force behind Motorola’s Optobus program has been to produce an optical interconnect that can beat copper solutions in both cost and performance. The resulting ‘link‘ consists of a pair of ten channel connectorized fiber ribbons and two multi-chip modules packaged as PGAs.

articleTitle: Laser-diode-based optoelectronic phase lock loops and their applications
publicationTitle: IEEE/LEOS 1995 Digest of the LEOS Summer Topical Meetings. Flat Panel Display Technology
abstract: Generation, control and measurement of electrical signals have benefited greatly from recent advances in optical technology. In particular, optoelectronically phase lock loops (OEPLL) are potentially useful devices for antenna remoting, optically fed wireless communication, and other applications involving optical-microwave interactions.
